newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Chinese dredge Nigerian river for smelter plant.
newsitem.headline: Chinese dredge Nigerian river for smelter plant.

text.p: Two Chinese companies are to start dredging the eastern Imo river to enable bigger vessels to carry finished products from an aluminium smelter being built in the area, a Chinese official said on Tuesday.

Yang Wensheng, assistant minister of foreign trade, quoted by the News Agency of Nigeria (NAN), told power and steel minister Bashir Dalhatu in Abuja that China would ensure the project was completed on schedule.
Yang, head of a visiting Chinese delegation, did not name the companies that would handle the dredging project.
Nigeria has been constructing the smelter in southeastern Ikot Abasi since 1990. It is expected to produce 180,000 tonnes of ingots and billets a year for local demand and exports.
In January Dalhatu said the government would commission the plant in March but industry sources said it is unlikely to be ready before the second quarter of the year.
The World Bank has said the project was ill-conceived and expensive. But the government said it expected the plant to earn much-needed hard currency and save on imports of ingots and billets.
Yang said China had submitted proposals for reactivating Nigeria's troubled steel projects in Aladja and Ajaokuta.
Dalhatu said the projects were part of government's effort to establish solid economic relations with China.
In 1995 both countries signed a $520 million contract in which state-run China Civil Engineering Construction (CCECC) would overhaul Nigeria's railways.

NAN said Shi Shenrui, vice president of CCECC, told transport minister Major-General Ibrahim Gumel on Monday in Lagos that it had completed the first phase and the target of October 1998 for the project would be met. --Lagos newsroom + 234 1 263 03 17
